(2) The clubface matches your spine angle (toe pointing up, not open to the sky or closed to the ground). (3) Your hands are in front of your chest, not behind you. If the club points right of target, you've taken it too far inside. If left, you've taken it outside. Practice: 10 slow-motion checkpoints, then 10 full swings trying to pass through the correct position. Use video to verify.

title: Halfway Back Drill #2
description: Setup: Take your address position with a mid-iron. Make a slow backswing and stop when your lead arm is parallel to the ground (halfway back). Execution: At this checkpoint, verify: (1) Your wrists have begun to hinge—the club shaft should form roughly a 90° angle with your lead arm (L-shape). (2) The club should point parallel to target line or SLIGHTLY left (for right-handers). If it points right of target, you've over-rotated the forearms. (3) The clubface should match your spine angle—not pointing at the sky (too open) or at the ground (too closed). Key feel: The hinge happens naturally as you rotate—don't force it. Practice: 10 slow-motion checkpoints with a mirror or video, then 10 full swings maintaining proper wrist set.

title: Split Hand Grip Drill (Rory McIlroy)
description: Work on feeling where the clubface & right elbow should be by holding the club normal in the left hand but then sliding the right hand further down the club

title: Putting Feel — Pendulum Stroke
description: The Feel: Imagine your shoulders and arms forming a triangle, with the putter hanging from this triangle. Your stroke is powered ONLY by your shoulders rocking—like a pendulum swinging from a fixed point. Your wrists stay completely quiet and passive throughout. Key checkpoints: (1) The triangle formed by shoulders/arms stays intact throughout the stroke. (2) Your backstroke length equals your through-stroke length (if you go back 6 inches, you go through 6 inches). (3) The pace is identical back and through—no acceleration or deceleration. (4) Your head and lower body stay perfectly still. Practice feel: Hold the putter lightly, let it swing freely, and feel your shoulder blades doing all the work while your hands are just along for the ride.

title: 80 Yards with 3 Different Clubs Game
description: Take your 3 wedges - lob, sand, gap and try and hit 80 yd shots 5 times in a row. Keep an eye on the ball flight and how much run out you get with each club

title: Find the Middle Drill
description: Setup: Apply foot spray, Dr. Scholl's spray, or impact tape to your clubface. Use a 7-iron. Execution: Hit 10 balls and check where each strike lands on the face. The spray/tape will show a clear impact mark. Goal: Consistently strike the CENTER of the face (the sweet spot). Common patterns to diagnose: (1) Toe hits = standing too far from ball or path too inside-out. (2) Heel hits = standing too close or over-the-top path. (3) High on face = ball position too far forward or hanging back. (4) Low on face = ball too far back or excessive forward shaft lean. After each shot, note the impact location, re-spray, and adjust. Track your progress: How many of 10 are center-face? Goal: 7+ center strikes. This drill reveals the truth about your ball striking.

title: Shank Shield Game
description: Create a two‑tee ‘no‑go zone’ just outside the ball on the heel side. Hit 10 balls scoring +2 for a center or toe strike, +1 for a green‑high result, 0 for slight heel contact without a shank, and −2 for any shank or tee strike. Play 3 rounds and try to beat your total each session. You can also use some sort of spray or sticker on the club to see where you are striking it.

title: Fire the Hips Feel
description: Arms outrace the lower body with a closed club face resulting in a hook. Feel the club stay at the top for a split second longer and fire the hips before starting your downswing

title: Top of Backswing Drill #2
description: Make practice swings stopping at the top to check if your wrists are fully hinged and the clubface is square to the target.

title: Shot-Pattern Catalogue Game
description: Hit multiple drives focusing on shaping shots left‑to‑right and right‑to‑left; record the results to understand your shot tendencies and plan course strategy.

title: Ball Below Feet Adjustment Drill
description: Set up on a sidehill lie with the ball below your feet and grip down on the club; flex your knees more to maintain balance and aim slightly left of target.

title: Top of Backswing Drill #3
description: Ensure your right elbow (for right‑handed players) is pointing down and not flying out at the top; keeps your swing compact and on plane.

title: Impact Drill #1
description: Setup: Address the ball with a 7-iron. Press your hands forward so the shaft leans toward the target (about 2-3 inches ahead of the ball). Your weight should favor your lead foot (60/40). Execution: Make three-quarter swings focusing on returning to this 'hands ahead' position at impact. The clubhead should strike the ball FIRST, then brush the turf AFTER. Checkpoint: At impact, your hands should be ahead of the clubhead, lead wrist flat or slightly bowed, and your belt buckle turning toward the target. Listen for sound: a compressed strike sounds solid like 'click', not thin like 'clack'. Hit 20 balls focusing solely on ball-first contact with forward shaft lean.

title: Alignment Stick in Belt Loops Drill
description: Slide an alignment stick through your belt loops so it runs across your hips. Make smooth half swings where your trail elbow clears the stick without hitting it. If you clip it, your lower body is outracing your upper body—common in hooks and blocks. Focus on turning your chest and hips together through impact for a synced, solid strike.

title: Hover the Club Feel
description: Before swinging, hover the clubhead slightly above the ground behind the ball to reduce tension and encourage a smooth takeaway.

title: Through the Gate Putting Drill
description: Set two tees a ball’s width apart a few feet in front of your ball and roll putts through them; ensures your starting line is correct and the putter face is square.

title: No Wrist Chipping Feel
description: Feel like you’re taking a putting stroke when chipping. Don’t engage the wrists. If you want it to go higher, open the club face, lower - ball back in stance and COMMIT. Don’t try to help the ball up in the air

title: Strike Check Alignment Drill
description: Use two tees forming a gate just wider than your clubhead and practise hitting shots without disturbing them; this checks clubface alignment and swing path.

title: Chipping Drill — Landing Spot Towel
description: Lay a small towel 3 paces on the green. Land 10 chips on the towel. Move it back 2 paces and repeat. Change lies and clubs.

title: Towel Under Arms Drill
description: Place a towel under both armpits and hit pitch shots without dropping it; keeps arms connected to the body and encourages body rotation.

title: Rhythm Sequencing Drill
description: Setup: Take your normal stance with a 7-iron. Execution: Make a backswing and PAUSE for a full count at the top ('one-one-thousand'). From the pause, let your lower body START first—feel your hips begin rotating toward the target while your arms and club stay back momentarily. Then let the arms follow naturally. The key is the sequence: hips lead, shoulders follow, arms trail behind. This creates proper 'lag' and prevents rushing. Rhythm check: Your downswing should feel smooth and unhurried, not quick. Practice 10 swings with the pause, then 10 without the pause but maintaining the same lower-body-first feel. Count 'back... pause... through' as you swing.

title: Gate Putting Drill
description: Setup: Place two tees in the ground about 1/4 inch wider than your putter head on each side, creating a 'gate.' Position them about 6 inches in front of your ball on your target line. The gate should be just wide enough for your putter to pass through cleanly. Execution: Make putting strokes, focusing on swinging the putter straight through the gate without touching either tee. If you hit the tee closest to you (inside), your stroke is pulling/cutting across the ball. If you hit the far tee (outside), you're pushing. Start with 3-foot putts and work back to 6 feet. Key feel: Feel like the putter face stays square and travels straight down the target line through the gate. Practice 20 strokes, then test yourself: make 5 consecutive clean passes through the gate. Goal: Groove a square, straight-back-straight-through stroke path for short putts.

title: Hit a cut
description: If you struggle with hooking the ball, figure out how to hit a cut 5 times & pay attention to what your body does. Think about keeping the clubface more open at impact (vs. closed), open your stance & your shoulders

title: Creating Lag with Alignment Stick
description: Place an alignment stick alongside the grip and extend it past your lead hip; practise swings without hitting your body to feel lag and late wrist release.

title: 9-Shot Chipping Challenge
description: Play nine different chip shots: bump‑and‑run, flop, uphill, downhill, from rough, tight lie, buried lie, over a bunker and sidehill. Score yourself on up‑and‑downs.

title: Thin Drill — Tee Under Ball Arc
description: Setup: Place a tee in the ground about 3-4 inches IN FRONT of your ball (toward the target), pushed down so only 1/4 inch is above ground. Use a 7 or 8-iron. Execution: Make swings with the goal of striking the ball first, then clipping the tee out of the ground on your follow-through. This ensures you're hitting DOWN on the ball with a descending blow, which cures thin/topped shots. If you hit the tee before the ball or miss the tee entirely, you're scooping or hanging back. Key feels: Keep your chest moving toward the target through impact, maintain spine angle, and feel like you're 'covering' the ball. Your divot should start AT or AFTER ball position. Hit 20 balls tracking ball-then-tee success rate.

title: Top of Backswing – Right Hand Position Drill
description: Check that your right hand is supporting the club at the top without tension; a relaxed trail hand allows the club to fully set.

title: Draw Feel — Close the door
description: Feel the lead hand "closing a door" through impact so the face is a touch more closed relative to path while keeping the path from the inside.

title: Hybrid Coin Drill
description: Setup: Place a coin (quarter works well) about 3-4 inches in front of your ball on the target line. Use your hybrid or fairway wood. Ball position should be slightly forward of center. Execution: Make your swing with the goal of striking the ball FIRST, then brushing the coin on your follow-through. This trains the slight descending blow needed for crisp hybrid/fairway wood contact. Common mistake: trying to help the ball up causes thin or topped shots. Key feels: Keep your chest moving through impact, maintain your spine angle, and feel like you're covering the ball with your chest. Hit 15-20 balls—success is ball-then-coin contact with a slight brush of turf after the ball.

title: Darts Chipping Game
description: Setup: Around the practice green, place a towel or small target as the 'bullseye' about 15 feet from an open area. Create scoring zones: within 1 club-length = 50 points, within 2 club-lengths = 30 points, within 3 club-lengths = 20 points, on the green but outside = 10 points, miss the green = 0 points. Scatter 10-12 balls at varying distances (10-40 yards) with different lies around the green. Execution: Chip each ball toward the target, keeping score like darts. Add up your total after all balls are played. Variations: Play against a friend (alternating shots), set a target score to beat (try for 300+), or add negative points (-20) for chips that roll off the green. Goal: Score 350+ points in a round. This game trains distance control and landing spot precision while adding competitive pressure.

title: Takeaway Stick Tip Drill
description: Place an alignment stick along your toe line and another across your chest; practise taking the club back so it stays parallel with the stick to groove a proper takeaway.

title: Tempo Town Feel
description: The “Tempo Town” feel is all about effortless rhythm, smooth, unhurried, and naturally flowing. Ernie Els and Vijay Singh make it look like the club swings them, not the other way around, with gravity guiding the motion. To emulate that silky rhythm, golfers can say “Ernie Els” or “Freddie Couples” as they swing, one syllable back and one through, to groove that same calm, balanced tempo.

title: Fairway Bunker Strike Drill
description: Setup: In a fairway bunker, dig your feet in SLIGHTLY (less than greenside bunker). Ball position center or slightly back. Choke down 1 inch on the grip. Take one more club than normal. Execution: Keep your lower body very QUIET throughout the swing—minimal leg action. Make a controlled 3/4 swing with smooth tempo. Focus on picking the ball CLEAN off the sand (ball first, minimal sand). Key differences from greenside bunker: (1) NO sand before the ball, (2) Quieter lower body to maintain height, (3) Swing easier—control is more important than power. Common mistake: digging feet in too deep, causing fat shots. Think 'sweep' not 'splash.' Hit 10-15 balls focusing on clean contact. Success = ball comes out clean with minimal sand spray. Listen for that clean 'click' sound at impact.

title: Head Against the Wall Drill
description: Stand with the side of your head lightly touching a wall while swinging; prevents swaying and encourages rotation around a stable axis.

title: Between the Markers
description: Set two markers a hole‑length apart creating a narrow lane. Putt through the lane without touching the markers; emphasises starting line and speed.

title: Transition Drill #3
description: Setup: Take your address position with a mid-iron. Make a full backswing to the top. Execution: From the top, focus on letting your arms DROP straight down while your lower body starts unwinding toward the target. The key feel: your arms fall passively while your hips rotate—like dropping your arms while turning. This prevents 'casting' (throwing the club from the top) which kills lag and power. Practice sequence: (1) Backswing to top, (2) Feel arms drop as dead weight, (3) Hips rotate simultaneously, (4) Club naturally falls into the slot. The club should feel like it's falling BEHIND you, not out toward the ball. Practice 10 slow-motion transitions without hitting, then 10 hitting at 50% speed. The ball should start slightly right with draw spin.

title: Chipping Ladder Drill (HackMotion)
description: Create landing zones at increasing distances and chip balls into each zone in order; improves distance control and touch.

title: Pinseeker Game
description: Choose a flag on the range and hit a set number of shots to it; score yourself based on how many shots finish within a specified distance of the flag.

title: Putter Head Stuck to the Ground Feel
description: Feel the putter head sticks low to the ground on the backswing for a consistent motion

title: Hands at Address Drill
description: Setup: Take your address position with a mid-iron. Check these two hand position fundamentals: Execution: (1) DISTANCE FROM BODY: With arms hanging relaxed, your hands should be about one hand-width (4-5 inches) away from your thighs. Too close = cramped swing, too far = reaching. (2) SHAFT ANGLE: The butt end of the club should point at your belt buckle (or just left of it for right-handers). If it points at your chest, you're standing too close; if it points below your belt, you're too far away. Checkpoints: Let your arms hang naturally, then grip the club—don't reach for it. Your arms should have a slight bend at the elbows. Practice: Set up, check position, step away, repeat 10 times until it's automatic. Take a photo to verify your positions match these checkpoints.

title: Around the World Putting
description: Place balls at four compass points around the hole (north, south, east, west) and try to make them consecutively; if you miss, start over. Place the balls 2-3 ft away

title: Thin Game — Center-Strike Ladder
description: Use face spray. Hit 10 shots trying to move strike from low to center in 3 steps. +1 for centered strike, 0 for slight miss, −1 for thin.

title: Putting Rule Drill
description: Setup: Lay a yardstick, metal ruler, or putting alignment rod flat on the practice green, pointing at a hole about 6-8 feet away. Place your ball at one end of the ruler. Execution: Stroke putts attempting to roll the ball along the ruler for its entire length before it drops off. If the ball falls off the side, your face angle was open or closed at impact, or your path was offline. This drill provides INSTANT feedback on face angle and starting line. Key technique: Keep the putter face perfectly square at impact, and start the ball on your intended line. Start by rolling balls along the ruler without a hole, just focusing on keeping the ball on the ruler. Progress to aiming at the hole. Goal: 5 consecutive putts that stay on the ruler the full length.

title: Slow Motion Balance Drill
description: Make slow full swings, concentrating on maintaining your balance throughout the swing; helps beginners feel proper weight shift and tempo.

title: Line in the Sand Game
description: In a bunker, draw a line a few inches behind the ball. Splash the sand so that the club enters on the line and propels the ball out; score based on proximity to the hole. Make sure you hear the thump at the bottom

title: Alignment Stick Ramp Drill
description: Place an alignment stick on the ground with one end raised; chip balls over the ramp to promote a higher launch and proper strike.

title: One-Handed Putting Drill
description: Both Tiger Woods and Jon Rahm use one-handed putting drills to sharpen feel and face control. By practicing with only the trail (right) hand, they isolate touch, tempo, and the natural release of the putter without interference from the lead hand. Tiger often pairs this with his classic tee-gate drill to ensure center-face contact and a square path, while Rahm focuses on rhythm and pure roll. The goal for both is the same — build confidence, consistency, and a smoother, more instinctive stroke under pressure.

title: Putting Game — Ladder to 3-Putt Proof
description: Putt from 20, 30, 40, 50 feet. Par is 2 putts. +1 for a 1‑putt. −1 for a 3‑putt. Play 12 holes and try to finish under par.

title: Swing to Right Field Feel
description: Feel like you are swinging the golf club out to right field in order to correct your slice. For golfers that tend to slice the ball you really want to exaggerate and you’ll be surprised that this barely gets you to a neutral swing path. Classic example of feel vs. real in the golf swing.

title: Hook Cure Alignment Drill
description: Set up two alignment sticks creating a gate with the ball in the middle and practise swinging through without touching them; corrects an in‑to‑out path that causes hooks.

title: Bowed Wrist Feel
description: Bow your wrist at the top of the backswing which helps you to shallow the golf club and get the club face closed at impact. The opposite with a cupped wrist tends to lead towards and open club face and weak slices. The other benefit is bowing the wrist give you a second to collect at the top of backswing and sequence correctly.

title: Hip Rotation Stick Drill
description: Thread an alignment stick through your belt loops and practise rotating your hips back and through while keeping the stick level; promotes proper hip turn and prevents sway.

title: Strike The Match Feel
description: Visualise striking a match at impact: imagine the clubface brushing the ground ahead of the ball, as though lighting a match; encourages descending strike and compression.

title: Align Your Body to Combat a Hook Feel
description: Alignment is the core of the golf swing. If you have a tendency to hook the ball, check your alignment. Feel like you open the stance a bit, open the hips and shoulders. Take your same swing and see how that impacts the golf ball. The same feel could be used for slicing.

title: Tempo Drill — Metronome 2:1
description: Use a metronome or count "one‑two". Takeaway to top is two counts. Top to impact is one. Keep balance and same rhythm as speed increases.

title: Fairway Bunker Drill
description: Setup: In a fairway bunker, position the ball slightly back of center in your stance. Dig your feet in LESS than a greenside bunker—you want a stable base but not too low. Choke down on the club about 1 inch and take one MORE club than normal (if you'd hit 7-iron, use 6-iron). Execution: Make a 3/4 swing focusing on picking the ball CLEAN—no sand before the ball. Key differences from greenside bunkers: (1) You WANT ball-first contact, (2) Keep your lower body quiet to maintain your height, (3) Swing easier than normal to maintain balance. Focus on making contact on the ball's equator or just below. Common mistake: taking sand first (causes fat shots that go nowhere). Hit 10-15 balls; success = clean contact with minimal sand.

title: One-Handed Bunker Drill
description: Setup: In a greenside bunker, grip your sand wedge with ONLY your trail hand (right hand for righties). Open the clubface and dig your feet into the sand for stability. Execution: Make bunker swings using only your trail hand, focusing on: (1) hinging your wrist fully in the backswing, (2) splashing the sand 2 inches behind the ball, and (3) letting the club slide under the ball without decelerating. The one-handed swing prevents over-powering and teaches proper wrist action and acceleration through the sand. Hit 10-15 shots one-handed, then add your lead hand and replicate the same feel. Goal: Develop soft, controlled bunker shots with proper bounce usage.

title: Belt Buckle at Target Feel
description: If you’re hitting it fat, think about getting all of the weight onto the front leg by feeling like your belt buckle is pointed to the target at impact. Fat shots come from impact & divot behind the ball. Try keeping your dominant eye on the front of the golf ball

title: Impact Drill #3
description: Setup: Get an impact bag (or use a heavy cushion, duffel bag filled with towels, or old tire). Place it where the ball would be. Execution: Make slow, controlled swings into the impact bag, freezing at impact. At this frozen position, check: (1) HANDS ahead of clubhead—the shaft leans toward the target, (2) Lead wrist flat or slightly bowed, (3) Hips open to target (30-40°), (4) Weight on lead foot (70%+), (5) Head behind the ball. Hold this position for 3 seconds, feeling the muscles engaged. This builds 'impact memory' in your body. Key benefit: Strengthens the correct impact position muscles and ingrains the feel of hands-ahead compression. Do 20 reps, holding each impact freeze for 3 seconds. Then hit balls replicating the same positions.

title: Cross-Handed Pitching Drill
description: Hit pitch shots with your lead hand below the trail hand (cross‑handed grip) to feel the correct shaft lean and stop flipping at impact.

title: Applying Pressure Ball Under Foot Drill
description: Place a golf ball or small object under the outside of your trail foot during the swing to feel pressure moving into your lead side; improves weight shift.

title: Parallel Set-Up Alignment Drill
description: Make sure your feet, knees, hips and shoulders are parallel to the target line; helps you aim correctly and promotes an on‑plane swing.

title: Three-Ball Rhythm Drill
description: Hit three balls consecutively with increasing swing lengths (half, three‑quarter, full) to build rhythm and tempo in your full swing.

title: Cover the Ball Feel
description: For crisp iron shots, get your weight and center of mass slightly forward at impact so that your chest “covers” the ball. This helps achieve a descending angle of attack and solid contact. One cause for thinning the golf shot is standing up through impact. Feeling like you cover the ball will force you to stay down

title: Fairway Game
description: Hit 18 tee shots toward a defined “fairway” (about 30–40 yds wide). Score +1 for landing in, 0 for slightly offline, –1 for OB. Create your fairway by picking two landmarks downrange (like flags or yardage signs) or by holding your fingers up to frame a fairway-sized window at your target. Go through your full pre-shot routine every time and track your total score—try to beat your personal best.

title: Top of Backswing Drill #1
description: At the top of your backswing, check that your lead arm is across your chest and the clubshaft is parallel to your target line; ensures a full turn.

title: Club Face Open Through Impact Feel
description: If you struggle with a hook, it could be because the clubface is closed at impact. Focus on a very square clubface erroring on the side of opening the clubface a hair at impact and see how that impacts the ball. The root cause is typically flipping at the bottom of the swing so maintain your wrist angle

title: Tee in Front of the Ball Drill
description: If you’re struggling with chunking the ball or pure contact, put a tee into the ground 1 in in front of the ball and feel like you’re hammering that tee into the ground with your clubface. This helps control low point

title: Drop the Bucket Drill
description: Squeeze an empty range bucket between your legs as you start your backswing. Drop the bucket to initiate the downswing, which gets you to fire your lower body first (opening your front side to target) thus promoting the correct swing sequencing. This help to naturally shallow the golf club and get it into the slow and promotes an in to out club path. Great driver drill for those that struggle with the slice.
